decision: Implement the complete M03 contract through one isolated code owner after parallel design exploration.
why: Tasks, commands, approvals and recovery share an end-to-end protocol and need one implementation contract.

decision: Ran the existing workspace tests before changing implementation.
why: Establish a passing migration, authentication and transport baseline before adding recovery.
result: Passed with actual M01 TCP and M02 TLS binaries.

decision: Selected Astra with all six independent-judge gates and Sol reducer, admission bounds and document retry identity.
why: The design separates stable intent, current delivery authority and durable effect evidence; the judge exposed claim, journal replacement and publication gaps.

decision: Implement M03 directly in the assigned isolated worktree after parent design rows from 2026-10-26T17:29:19Z through 2026-10-26T17:37:52Z.
why: The parent owns review and PR work; nested agents are prohibited.

decision: Captured actual manager rejection of the durable recovery request before implementation.
why: The acceptance must distinguish M03 from the previous binaries.
result: Failed with HTTP 404 instead of durable submission HTTP 200.

decision: Implemented one manager task owner, atomic command and event writes, stable owner approvals, and source-driven Markdown recovery.
why: Task state and authority must survive login-session deletion and transport replacement.
result: All 15 manager unit tests passed, including populated version-two migration and transaction rollback.

decision: Added bounded report and inventory recovery, single-use execution claims, and an independent durable synthetic effect ledger.
why: Separate durable effect evidence exposes the crash window and detects blind retries.
result: Ten recovery scenarios and focused updated session and fencing fixtures passed.

decision: Separated database privacy checks from the 64-kibibyte secret-file reader and canonicalized private SQLite paths.
why: Actual worker restart exposed WAL size refusal and macOS temporary-directory symlinks; database metadata needs the same ownership checks without the secret payload limit.
result: Restart recovery passed without weakening secret-file size limits.

decision: Replay pending reports in sequence before returning a repeated terminal outcome.
why: Returning the terminal report alone could skip unacknowledged progress and force a reconnect.
result: Repeated delivery retains one provider invocation and its original result report identity.

decision: Recheck queued deliveries at the manager and expire a worker claim after five seconds without its permit.
why: A consumed permit discarded during a control change must not leave the worker pending forever or admit later replacement work.
result: Stale and timed-out permits produce no extra ledger invocation.

decision: Rebuilt base 3102400 in a temporary source archive and tested durable recovery after its actual daemon restart.
why: The first baseline failed at the missing task API; a historical binary restart gives direct evidence of the original lost-outcome behavior.
result: Expected assertion failed with unknown_task instead of the original completed result. The script verified Cargo exit 101.
